subject: OroAI — dedicated capacity & footprint interview
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Das <samira@oro.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 15:08:00 +0000
Subject: OroAI — dedicated capacity & footprint interview

Hi Samira,

Thanks for taking the call last week. To turn that conversation into a scoped Dedicated proposal we need a quick traffic + token profile from your side so we can map to GPU counts and a preliminary cost/latency tradeoff. I attached our lightweight template (redwood_pre-sales_template_v2.xlsx) — if you can fill the highlighted sheets it covers most of what we need.

Quick ask list (can respond inline or attach a CSV):
- Baseline qps (avg) and peak qps (1m/10m window)
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p95) per route/service
- Prompt & response token distribution (avg / 90th pct)
- Streaming vs non-streaming preference + percent of requests that stream
- Multi-tenant breakdown: top 5 tenants and % of traffic each
- Typical session length / KV-cache reuse expectations
- Any preferred model families / max model size you plan to serve
- Compliance constraints (retention, logging, region)

If easier, send a 48–72 hour traffic snapshot (CSV) and we’ll turn it into an initial sizing. We’re aiming to produce a preliminary fleet sketch by end of week.

Thanks — attaching template.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_pre-sales_template_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Samira Das <samira@oro.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Ruiz <miguel@oro.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:24:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OroAI — dedicated capacity & footprint interview

Hi Jonas — thanks, attaching a 72-hour snapshot (oro_traffic_snapshot.csv) and a short answers doc inline.

Baseline / peaks:
- Avg qps: ~18 requests/sec across our public inference endpoint (measured over last 72h).
- Peak (1m): 720 qps (we saw a 10-minute burst last Wed, sustained ~600–700 for ~8 minutes).

Latency targets:
- Target p50: 80–120 ms (we’re fine).
- Target p95: 200 ms (hard requirement for UI flows).

Token profile:
- Prompt avg: 45 tokens (90th: 130)
- Response avg: 220 tokens (90th: 560)
- ~12% of requests are very short (prompt < 15 tokens, response < 40) for metadata lookups.

Streaming / caching:
- ~55% of requests use streaming (progressive responses to web clients).
- KV cache reuse estimate: 70–80% for repeated user prompts (we have a lot of prefix reuse).

Multi-tenant split (top 3):
- Tenant A — 42%
- Tenant B — 14%
- Tenant C — 9%
(rest are small internal/test tenants)

Model family / constraints:
- Plan to serve a QLoRA fine-tuned variant of an open-70B family (latency-sensitive; prefer 7-bit quantized runtime).
- Data residency: US-only for now.

Other notes:
- We have a soft SLA requirement: 99.9% availability per month.
- We can tolerate occasional fallbacks to a smaller model during extreme contention (as long as UI has graceful messaging).

Attachment: oro_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up to walk through the CSV.

Best,
Samira
VP Product, OroAI
samira@oro.ai

Jonas / Karthik — quick clarifying questions (adding Samira so she can confirm):

- Is the model inference configured to use streaming chunk sizes ~64 tokens or larger? That affects batching and tail latency.
- Do they expect KV-cache warm start on every request (session affinity) or will requests be mostly stateless?
- Any preference on GPU family? (A100 vs H100 vs inferred mixed pool). If they prefer quantized runtime on A100-80GB we can size differently than H100.
- Do they have a hard constraint on cold-start latency for autoscale events?

If Samira can reply inline we’ll fold answers into the initial sketch.

From: Samira Das <samira@oro.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Ruiz <miguel@oro.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OroAI — dedicated capacity & footprint interview

Hi Marissa, Jonas — answers below, inline to your bullets.

> Is the model inference configured to use streaming chunk sizes ~64 tokens or larger?
We stream at ~80 token chunks by default for UX pacing. Occasional long completions stream in 120–160 token chunks.

> Do they expect KV-cache warm start on every request (session affinity) or will requests be mostly stateless?
About 75% of requests hit a warm KV cache (session affinity), the rest are stateless API calls. We do keep session ids in metadata and prefer affinity where possible.

> Any preference on GPU family?
We prefer a cost-effective 7-bit workflow; A100 40GB or 80GB depending on memory. We are open to H100 for the highest headroom but would like Redwood’s recommendation on p99 tail behavior.

> Hard constraint on cold-start latency for autoscale?
We need cold-starts for new model replicas to be < 3s for background scale-ups and < 600ms for hot replacement paths (if using warm spare capacity).

Other attachment: we have a short SLA/requirements doc (SLA attached).

—
Samira Das
VP Product, OroAI
samira@oro.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2028 20:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OroAI — dedicated capacity & footprint interview

Samira / Miguel — thanks for the speedy responses and the snapshot. Summary & next steps from our side:

- Preliminary sizing note: given avg qps ~18, peak 700+ for short bursts, streaming ~55% and prompt/response token mix (45/220 avg) we’ll prototype a mixed pool: principally A100-80GB for quantized 70B runtime plus a small H100 pool for peak overflow and canary testing.
- Autoscale recommendation: reserve warm spares to meet the <600ms hot replacement requirement; fallback policies to a lighter quantized variant for extreme peaks.
- KV-cache: we’ll assume 75% locality and size memory for a high hit-rate profile to reduce per-token compute.

Deliverables & timing:
- By EOD Mon (2028-07-15) we’ll share a preliminary PDF estimate with GPU counts, expected token-hour cost, and a latency overlay (redwood-estimate-oro-dedicated-v1.pdf).
- Schedule: can we do a 45m sizing walkthrough Tue 2028-07-16 16:00–16:45 PT? (I included a scheduler link).

Please let me know if any of the assumptions above are incorrect and I’ll adjust the sizing. If that time works I’ll send a calendar invite and attach the draft estimate.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-estimate-oro-dedicated-v1.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
